title: Blueberry and lemon tart
subtitle: summer blueberry and lemon curd tart
excerpt: A blueberry and lemon tart fills a blind-baked pastry case with lemon curd and tops it with fresh blueberries that are briefly heated in a jam glaze to make them glisten. The lemon curd provides the sharpness; the blueberries provide sweetness and colour. It takes about 45 minutes once the pastry is baked and requires no further time in the oven.
sourceNotes: Lemon curd tarts filled with fresh berries, rather than baked with the berries as in a traditional fruit tart, represent a French-influenced British home baking style popularised through the 1990s and 2000s. The method of filling a pre-baked pastry case with a no-bake filling and dressing the top with fresh fruit is the same approach used in classic strawberry tarts (tarte aux fraises), adapted here to blueberries and lemon. Blueberries became widely available in British supermarkets from the mid-1980s onward through imports and later domestic cultivation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the pastry case up to 1 day ahead. Fill and decorate on the day of serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: for blind baking the pastry case only

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 190°C for blind baking; the lemon curd filling is not baked in the oven

content.text: Blueberry and lemon tart works because the lemon curd's acidity balances the sweetness of the blueberries. The pastry case is baked and cooled, filled with lemon curd, then topped with fresh blueberries glazed in warmed jam. The result requires no further oven time and comes together quickly once the pastry is done.
Make and blind bake the pastry

Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar to fine crumbs. Add the egg yolk and cold water, bring together into a dough, wrap and refrigerate 30 minutes. Roll to 3 mm, line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, and refrigerate 20 minutes. Blind bake at 190°C with baking beans for 15 minutes, then without for 10 minutes until fully dry and pale gold. Cool completely.
Fill and top with glazed blueberries

Spoon the lemon curd into the cooled pastry case and spread it level to just below the rim. Scatter the blueberries over the curd in a single layer. Warm the jam in a small saucepan with 1 teaspoon of water until it becomes a fluid glaze. Brush or spoon the warm glaze over the blueberries to coat them. Refrigerate the tart for at least 1 hour before serving to allow the curd to firm slightly. Serve the same day.
